tool_proficiencies: one type of artisan's tools of your choice

1.name: Rage
1.description: In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. On your turn, you can enter a rage as a bonus action. While raging, you gain the following benefits if you aren’t wearing heavy armor: advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws; when you make a melee weapon attack using Strength, you gain a bonus to the damage roll that increases as you gain levels as a barbarian; you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. If you are able to cast spells, you can’t cast them or concentrate on them while raging. Your rage lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are knocked unconscious or if your turn ends and you haven’t attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then. You can also end your rage on your turn as a bonus action. Once you have raged the number of times shown for your barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian table, you must finish a long rest before you can rage again.

restrictions.details: Cannot cast or concentrate on spells while raging.

1.name: Unarmored Defense (Barbarian)
1.description: While you are not wearing any armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

2.name: Reckless Attack
2.description: Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

2.name: Danger Sense
2.description: At 2nd level, you gain an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren’t as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge away from danger. You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects that you can see, such as traps and spells. To gain this benefit, you can’t be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.

effects.notes: Player must not be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated. Assumes saving throw source will be tagged 'visible_source' or with 'trap'/'spell' by the system resolving the save.

3.name: Primal Path
3.description: At 3rd level, you choose a path that shapes the nature of your rage. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th levels.

5.name: Extra Attack
5.description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

5.name: Fast Movement
5.description: Starting at 5th level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren’t wearing heavy armor.

6.name: Path Feature
6.description: Feature from your chosen Primal Path.

7.name: Feral Instinct
7.description: By 7th level, your instincts are so honed that you have advantage on initiative rolls. Additionally, if you are surprised at the beginning of combat and aren’t incapacitated, you can act normally on your first turn if you enter your rage before doing anything else on that turn.

effects.name: Feral Instinct Surprise Rage
effects.details: If surprised and not incapacitated, can act normally on first turn by raging first. Requires surprise and initiative system integration.

9.name: Brutal Critical (1 die)
9.description: Beginning at 9th level, you can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack.

10.name: Path Feature
10.description: Feature from your chosen Primal Path.

11.name: Relentless Rage
11.description: Starting at 11th level, your rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 hit points while you’re raging and don’t die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, you drop to 1 hit point instead. Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a short or long rest, the DC resets to 10.

effects.name: Relentless Rage
effects.notes: Relentless Rage. This is a passive trigger, not an action ability.

13.name: Brutal Critical (2 dice)
13.description: At 13th level, you can roll two additional weapon damage dice when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack.

14.name: Path Feature
14.description: Feature from your chosen Primal Path.

15.name: Persistent Rage
15.description: Beginning at 15th level, your rage is so fierce that it ends early only if you fall unconscious or if you choose to end it.

17.name: Brutal Critical (3 dice)
17.description: At 17th level, you can roll three additional weapon damage dice when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack.

18.name: Indomitable Might
18.description: Beginning at 18th level, if your total for a Strength check is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.

effects.notes: Indomitable Might. Applied by ability check resolution system.

20.name: Primal Champion
20.description: At 20th level, you embody the power of the wilds. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4. Your maximum for those scores is now 24.

tool_proficiencies: three musical instruments of your choice

College of Lore.description: Bards of the College of Lore know something about most things, collecting bits of knowledge from sources as diverse as scholarly tomes and peasant tales.

3.name: Bonus Proficiencies (Lore)
3.description: When you join the College of Lore at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in three skills of your choice.

effects.notes: College of Lore - Choose 3 skill proficiencies.

3.name: Cutting Words
3.description: Also at 3rd level, you learn how to use your wit to distract, confuse, and otherwise sap the confidence and competence of others. When a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a damage roll, you can use your reaction to expend one of your uses of Bardic Inspiration, roll the Bardic Inspiration die, and subtract the number rolled from the creature's roll. You can choose to use this feature after the creature makes its roll, but before the DM determines whether the attack roll or ability check succeeds or fails, or before the creature deals its damage. The creature is immune if it can't hear you or if it's immune to being charmed.

effects.name: Cutting Words
effects.notes: Uses Bardic Inspiration die. Complex reaction.

6.name: Additional Magical Secrets (Lore)
6.description: At 6th level, you learn two spells of your choice from any class. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the Bard table, or a cantrip. The chosen spells count as bard spells for you but don’t count against the number of bard spells you know.

effects.notes: College of Lore - Additional Magical Secrets. These do not count against spells known.

14.name: Peerless Skill
14.description: Starting at 14th level, when you make an ability check, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration. Roll a Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to your ability check. You can choose to do so after you roll the die for the ability check, but before the DM tells you whether you succeed or fail.

effects.name: Peerless Skill
effects.details: Can expend Bardic Inspiration use to add die to own ability check.
effects.notes: Activated on ability check, before outcome known.

College of Valor.description: Bards of the College of Valor are daring skalds whose tales keep alive the memory of the great heroes of the past, and thereby inspire a new generation of heroes.

3.name: Bonus Proficiencies (Valor)
3.description: When you join the College of Valor at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons.

3.name: Combat Inspiration
3.description: Also at 3rd level, you learn to inspire others in battle. A creature that has a Bardic Inspiration die from you can roll that die and add the number rolled to a weapon damage roll it just made. Alternatively, when an attack roll is made against the creature, it can use its reaction to roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to its AC against that attack, after seeing the roll but before knowing whether it hits or misses.
3.notes: Modifies Bardic Inspiration. The target can use the die for weapon damage OR AC (reaction).

effects.name: Bardic Inspiration
effects.notes: Valor Bard version of Inspiration. Die type scales with main BI feature.

6.name: Extra Attack (Valor)
6.description: Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

14.name: Battle Magic
14.description: At 14th level, you have mastered the art of weaving spellcasting and weapon use into a single harmonious act. When you use your action to cast a bard spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

1.name: Bardic Inspiration
1.description: You can inspire others through stirring words or music. To do so, you use a bonus action on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die, a d6. Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. The creature can wait until after it rolls the d20 before deciding to use the Bardic Inspiration die, but must decide before the DM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Once the Bardic Inspiration die is rolled, it is lost. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.

effects.name: Bardic Inspiration
effects.notes: Bardic Inspiration die is d6 at L1. Uses = CHA mod (min 1). Target gets the die.

2.name: Jack of All Trades
2.description: Starting at 2nd level, you can add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to any ability check you make that doesn’t already include your proficiency bonus.

effects.notes: Applies to ability checks that don't already include proficiency bonus.

2.name: Song of Rest (d6)
2.description: Beginning at 2nd level, you can use soothing music or oration to help revitalize your wounded allies during a short rest. If you or any friendly creatures who can hear your performance regain hit points at the end of the short rest by spending one or more Hit Dice, each of those creatures regains an extra 1d6 hit points.

effects.notes: Extra healing on short rest if HD are spent. Ally effect deferred.

3.name: Bard College
3.description: At 3rd level, you delve into the advanced techniques of a bard college of your choice.

3.name: Expertise (Bard L3)
3.description: At 3rd level, choose two of your skill proficiencies. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.

5.name: Bardic Inspiration (d8)
5.description: Your Bardic Inspiration die changes to a d8.

5.name: Font of Inspiration
5.description: Beginning when you reach 5th level, you regain all of your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a short or long rest.
5.notes: This feature modifies the 'Bardic Inspiration' ability to refresh on short_or_long_rest. The override above handles this.

6.name: Countercharm
6.description: At 6th level, you gain the ability to use musical notes or words of power to disrupt mind-influencing effects. As an action, you can start a performance that lasts until the end of your next turn. During that time, you and any friendly creatures within 30 feet of you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed. A creature must be able to hear you to gain this benefit. The performance ends early if you are incapacitated or silenced or if you voluntarily end it (no action required).

effects.name: Countercharm
effects.notes: Grants advantage vs frightened/charmed to allies in 30ft aura. Complex effect.

9.name: Song of Rest (d8)
9.description: Your Song of Rest die changes to a d8.

effects.notes: Song of Rest now uses d8.

10.name: Bardic Inspiration (d10)
10.description: Your Bardic Inspiration die changes to a d10.

10.name: Expertise (Bard L10)
10.description: At 10th level, choose two more of your skill proficiencies. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.

effects.notes: Choose 2 more skill proficiencies for Expertise.

10.name: Magical Secrets (L10)
10.description: By 10th level, you have plundered magical knowledge from a wide spectrum of disciplines. Choose two spells from any classes, including this one. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the Bard table, or a cantrip. The chosen spells count as bard spells for you and are included in the number in the Spells Known column of the Bard table.

effects.notes: Choose 2 spells of up to your max castable Bard spell level from any class list.

13.name: Song of Rest (d10)
13.description: Your Song of Rest die changes to a d10.

effects.notes: Song of Rest now uses d10.

14.name: Magical Secrets (L14)
14.description: Choose two additional spells from any class, up to the level you can cast.

15.name: Bardic Inspiration (d12)
15.description: Your Bardic Inspiration die changes to a d12.

17.name: Song of Rest (d12)
17.description: Your Song of Rest die changes to a d12.

effects.notes: Song of Rest now uses d12.

18.name: Magical Secrets (L18)
18.description: Choose two additional spells from any class, up to the level you can cast.

20.name: Superior Inspiration
20.description: At 20th level, when you roll initiative and have no uses of Bardic Inspiration left, you regain one use.

effects.name: Superior Inspiration
effects.notes: Regain 1 Bardic Inspiration if none left at initiative.

1.name: Divine Domain
1.description: Choose one domain related to your deity. This choice grants you domain spells and other features.

2.name: Channel Divinity
2.description: You gain the ability to channel divine energy. You have one use of this feature. You regain expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.
2.notes: This is the resource pool for various Channel Divinity options.

2.name: Channel Divinity: Turn Undead
2.description: As an action, you present your holy symbol and speak a prayer censuring the undead. Each undead that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.

effects.name: Turn Undead
effects.notes: Uses one charge of Channel Divinity.

5.name: Destroy Undead (CR 1/2)
5.description: When an undead fails its saving throw against your Turn Undead feature, the creature is instantly destroyed if its challenge rating is at or below 1/2.

6.name: Channel Divinity (2 uses)
6.description: You can use Channel Divinity twice between rests.

10.name: Divine Intervention
10.description: Beginning at 10th level, you can call on your deity to intervene on your behalf when your need is great.

18.name: Channel Divinity (3 uses)
18.description: You can use Channel Divinity three times between rests.

Life Domain.description: The Life domain focuses on the vibrant positive energy – one of the fundamental forces of the universe – that sustains all life.

1.name: Bonus Proficiency (Life)
1.description: You gain proficiency with heavy armor.

1.name: Disciple of Life
1.description: Your healing spells are more effective. Whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore hit points to a creature, the creature regains additional hit points equal to 2 + the spell’s level.

effects.name: Disciple of Life
effects.notes: Bonus healing to target when casting healing spell.

2.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
2.description: As an action, you present your holy symbol and evoke healing energy that can restore a total number of hit points equal to five times your cleric level. Choose any creatures within 30 feet of you, and divide these hit points among them. This feature can restore a creature to no more than half of its hit point maximum. You can’t use this feature on an undead or a construct.

6.name: Blessed Healer
6.description: Beginning at 6th level, the healing spells you cast on others heal you as well. When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you regain hit points equal to 2 + the spell’s level.

8.name: Divine Strike (Life)
8.description: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

17.name: Supreme Healing
17.description: Starting at 17th level, when you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, you instead use the highest number possible for each die.

Light Domain.description: Gods of light – including Helios, Lathander, and Pholtus – promote the ideals of rebirth and renewal, truth, vigilance, and beauty, often using the symbol of the Sun.

1.name: Bonus Cantrip (Light)
1.description: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain the light cantrip if you don’t already know it.

1.name: Warding Flare
1.description: Also at 1st level, you can interpose divine light between yourself and an attacking enemy. When you are attacked by a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll, causing light to flare before the attacker before it hits or misses. An attacker that can’t be blinded is immune to this feature. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

2.name: Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn
2.description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to harness sunlight, banishing darkness and dealing radiant damage to your foes.

6.name: Improved Flare
6.description: Starting at 6th level, you can also use your Warding Flare feature when a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you attacks a creature other than you.

8.name: Potent Spellcasting (Light)
8.description: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

17.name: Corona of Light
17.description: Starting at 17th level, you can use your action to activate an aura of sunlight that lasts for 1 minute or until you dismiss it using another action. You emit bright light in a 60-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. Your enemies in the bright light have disadvantage on saving throws against any spell that deals fire or radiant damage.

Fighter.description: A master of martial combat, skilled with a variety of weapons and armor. Fighters are versatile warriors who can adapt to any battlefield.
Fighter.primary_ability_description: Strength (STR) enhances your attack and damage with melee weapons. Dexterity (DEX) can be used for finesse weapons and improves Armor Class with lighter armors. Constitution (CON) increases your hit points, making you more durable.

1.name: Fighting Style
1.description: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

available_choices.name: Archery
available_choices.description: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.

available_choices.name: Defense
available_choices.description: While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

available_choices.name: Dueling
available_choices.description: When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

available_choices.name: Great Weapon Fighting
available_choices.description: When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.

available_choices.name: Protection
available_choices.description: When a creature you can see attacks a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll. You must be wielding a shield.

available_choices.name: Two-Weapon Fighting
available_choices.description: When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

1.name: Second Wind
1.description: You have a limited well of stamina that you can draw on to protect yourself from harm. On your turn, you can use this ability to regain hit points equal to 1d10 + your fighter level. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

2.name: Action Surge
2.description: Starting at 2nd level, you can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

5.name: Extra Attack
5.description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

9.name: Indomitable
9.description: Beginning at 9th level, you can reroll a saving throw that you fail. If you do so, you must use the new roll, and you can’t use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

11.name: Extra Attack (2)
11.description: At 11th level, you can attack three times when you take the Attack action.

13.name: Indomitable (two uses)
13.description: At 13th level, you gain a second use of Indomitable between long rests.

17.name: Action Surge (two uses)
17.description: Beginning at 17th level, you can use Action Surge twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.

17.name: Indomitable (three uses)
17.description: At 17th level, you gain a third use of Indomitable between long rests.

20.name: Extra Attack (3)
20.description: At 20th level, you can attack four times when you take the Attack action.

Battle Master.description: A Battle Master uses special combat maneuvers to control the battlefield and enhance their attacks.

3.name: Combat Superiority
3.description: You learn maneuvers that are fueled by special dice called superiority dice.

Champion.description: The Champion archetype focuses on the raw power of physical prowess, hitting harder and more often.

3.name: Improved Critical
3.description: Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

7.name: Remarkable Athlete
7.description: You can add half your proficiency bonus (round up) to any Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution check that doesn't already use your proficiency bonus. Also, your running long jump distance increases by your Strength modifier.

effects.name: Remarkable Athlete
effects.details: Half proficiency to unproficient STR/DEX/CON checks; STR_mod to long jump distance.

10.name: Additional Fighting Style
10.description: You gain an additional fighting style from the fighter list.

15.name: Superior Critical
15.description: Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 18, 19, or 20.

18.name: Survivor
18.description: At the start of each of your turns, you regain hit points equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier if you have no more than half of your hit points left. You don’t gain this benefit if you have 0 hit points.

Eldritch Knight.description: The Eldritch Knight combines martial mastery with the careful study of magic.

tool_proficiencies: one type of artisan's tools or one musical instrument

Path of the Berserker.description: The Path of the Berserker is a path of untamed fury, slick with blood. As you enter the berserker’s rage, you thrill in the chaos of battle, heedless of your own health or well-being.

3.name: Frenzy
3.description: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you can go into a frenzy when you rage. If you do so, for the duration of your rage you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one. When your rage ends, you suffer one level of exhaustion.

6.name: Mindless Rage
6.description: Beginning at 6th level, you can’t be charmed or frightened while raging. If you are charmed or frightened when you enter your rage, the effect is suspended for the duration of the rage.

10.name: Intimidating Presence
10.description: Beginning at 10th level, you can use your action to frighten someone with your menacing presence. When you do so, choose one creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to extend the duration of this effect on the frightened creature until the end of your next turn. This effect ends if the creature ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you.

14.name: Retaliation
14.description: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature.

Rogue.description: A cunning and elusive adventurer, relying on stealth, skill, and trickery. Rogues excel at finding and disabling traps, picking locks, and striking when least expected.
Rogue.primary_ability_description: Dexterity (DEX) is your most important ability, affecting your Armor Class, attack and damage with finesse or ranged weapons, and many of your crucial skills. Constitution (CON) boosts your hit points.

1.name: Expertise (1)
1.description: Choose two of your skill proficiencies, or one of your skill proficiencies and your proficiency with thieves' tools. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.

1.name: Sneak Attack
1.description: Beginning at 1st level, you know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll. The attack must use a finesse or a ranged weapon. You don't need advantage on the attack roll if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn't incapacitated, and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll. The amount of the extra damage increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue table.

1.name: Thieves' Cant
1.description: During your rogue training you learned thieves' cant, a secret mix of dialect, jargon, and code that allows you to hide messages in seemingly normal conversation.

2.name: Cunning Action
2.description: Your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act swiftly. Starting at 2nd level, you can take a bonus action on each of your turns in combat. This action can be used only to take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.

Thief.description: Thieves hone their skills in the subtler arts of larceny, stealth, and infiltration.

3.name: Fast Hands
3.description: You can use the bonus action granted by your Cunning Action to make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, use your thieves' tools to disarm a trap or open a lock, or take the Use an Object action.

3.name: Second-Story Work
3.description: Climbing no longer costs you extra movement. When you make a running long jump, the distance you cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Dexterity modifier.

9.name: Supreme Sneak
9.description: You have advantage on a Dexterity (Stealth) check if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.

13.name: Use Magic Device
13.description: You ignore all class, race, and level requirements on the use of magic items.

17.name: Thief's Reflexes
17.description: You take two turns during the first round of combat: one at your normal initiative, and a second at your initiative minus 10. You can't use this if surprised.

Wizard.description: A scholarly magic-user who studies the arcane arts to manipulate reality. Wizards command powerful spells through intellect and preparation.
Wizard.primary_ability_description: Intelligence (INT) is your key ability, determining the power of your spells, the number of spells you can prepare, and your spell attack bonus and save DC. Constitution (CON) helps you maintain concentration on spells and increases your hit points.

known_cantrips.name: Fire Bolt
known_cantrips.description: You hurl a mote of fire at a creature or object within range.

known_cantrips.name: Ray of Frost
known_cantrips.description: A frigid beam of blue-white light streaks toward a creature within range. On a hit, it takes 1d8 cold damage, and its speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

1.name: Initial Spellbook
1.description: You start with a spellbook containing six 1st-level wizard spells of your choice.
